title: Still Life & Flowers
description: Quiet arrangements of fruit, flowers, and objects — beauty in the everyday.

items.title: Still Life with Flowers
items.description_narrative: This oil on canvas by Odilon Redon presents a vibrant arrangement of flowers in a still life composition. Executed in 1905, it reflects the artist's later period of rich color and evocative forms.
items.tags: still life, flowers, oil painting, symbolist, evocative, vibrant, 20th century

items.title: Still Life with Flowers
items.description_narrative: This oil on canvas painting by Henri Fantin-Latour masterfully depicts a traditional still life composition focused on a vibrant bouquet of flowers. Executed in 1881, the artwork showcases the artist's signature attention to detail and texture, capturing the delicate beauty of the blossoms.
items.tags: still life, flowers, oil painting, realism, 19th century, floral, nature

items.title: Trompe-l'Oeil Still Life with a Flower Garland and a Curtain
items.description_narrative: Adriaen van der Spelt's *Trompe-l'Oeil Still Life with a Flower Garland and a Curtain* masterfully employs illusionistic techniques to deceive the viewer's eye. This oil on panel painting presents a detailed flower garland and a seemingly drawn-back curtain, creating a three-dimensional effect.
items.tags: still life, trompe l'oeil, illusionistic, flowers, curtain, Dutch, realism

items.title: Magnolias on Light Blue Velvet Cloth
items.description_narrative: Martin Johnson Heade captures the delicate beauty of magnolias arranged upon a light blue velvet cloth. The work emphasizes the pristine white petals and the rich texture of the drapery, creating a moment of serene stillness.
items.tags: still life, flower painting, magnolias, nature, american art, oil painting, serene

items.title: For Sunday's Dinner
items.description_narrative: William Michael Harnett's 'For Sunday's Dinner' presents a meticulously arranged still life, showcasing everyday objects and foodstuffs. This oil on canvas masterfully employs trompe l'oeil techniques to create an illusion of tangible reality, inviting viewers to closely inspect its detailed surfaces.
items.tags: still life, realism, trompe l'oeil, everyday objects, food, domestic, american art, late 19th century

items.title: The Irish Question
items.description_narrative: This intricate trompe l'oeil painting by De Scott Evans meticulously renders various documents and everyday objects, creating a convincing illusion of depth. The arrangement of a newspaper, pipe, and other ephemera subtly references the complex political and social issues surrounding the Irish question during the 1880s.
items.tags: trompe l'oeil, political, illusion, still life, american, 19th century

items.title: Chrysanthemums
items.description_narrative: Pierre-Auguste Renoir's 'Chrysanthemums' captures the vibrant beauty of a floral arrangement with characteristic Impressionist brushwork. Executed in oil on canvas, the painting emphasizes light and color, showcasing the delicate textures and rich hues of the blooms.
items.tags: chrysanthemums, flowers, still life, impressionism, french art, vibrant, delicate

items.title: Still Life with Dead Game, Fruits, and Vegetables in a Market
items.description_narrative: This expansive oil painting by Frans Snyders depicts a lavish market scene overflowing with dead game, a variety of fruits, and an assortment of vegetables. The composition showcases a mastery of texture and abundance, typical of the opulent still life tradition.
items.tags: still life, dead game, market scene, fruits, vegetables, baroque, flemish art, opulence

items.title: Just Dessert
items.description_narrative: William Michael Harnett's "Just Dessert" is an oil on canvas painting from 1891. Harnett was renowned for his meticulously rendered still life compositions, often employing trompe l'oeil techniques to create the illusion of reality.
items.tags: still life, trompe l'oeil, american art, 19th century, realism, oil painting

items.title: Still Life with Monkey, Fruits, and Flowers
items.description_narrative: Jean-Baptiste Oudry's 'Still Life with Monkey, Fruits, and Flowers' showcases a vibrant array of natural elements, anchored by a lively monkey amidst abundant produce and blossoms. This richly detailed oil painting captures the texture and vitality of its subjects, demonstrating the artist's skill in animal and still-life genres.
items.tags: still life, monkey, fruits, flowers, rococo, animal painting, nature, baroque

items.title: Apples and Grapes
items.description_narrative: Claude Monet's 'Apples and Grapes' presents a vibrant still life, capturing the interplay of light and color on the fruit. Rendered in oil on canvas, this 1880 work exemplifies the artist's Impressionistic approach to capturing everyday subjects with fresh immediacy.
items.tags: apples, grapes, still life, impressionism, french art, oil painting, fruit

items.title: Still Life
items.description_narrative: This still life by Pieter Claesz meticulously renders everyday objects, often including pewter, glass, and foodstuffs, inviting close observation of texture and light. Such works, painted with subtle tonality, exemplify the quiet domesticity and material prosperity often depicted in Dutch Golden Age art.
items.tags: still life, realism, dutch golden age, objects, domestic scene, oil painting

items.title: Thistles
items.description_narrative: John Singer Sargent's 'Thistles' offers a detailed study of the plant, rendered in oil on canvas. Painted between 1883 and 1889, this work exemplifies the artist's expressive brushwork and keen observation of nature.
items.tags: thistles, botanical study, nature, oil painting, american art, late 19th century

items.title: Apples
items.description_narrative: Henri Matisse's 'Apples' is an oil on canvas painting created in 1916. It exemplifies the artist's continuous exploration of still life subjects.
items.tags: still life, apples, oil painting, modern art, Henri Matisse

items.title: Roses in a Bowl
items.description_narrative: Henri Fantin-Latour's 'Roses in a Bowl' captures the delicate beauty of a floral arrangement with meticulous detail. This oil on canvas painting from 1881 exemplifies the artist's mastery of still life, presenting the roses with a soft, naturalistic elegance.
items.tags: roses, flowers, still life, naturalism, realism, elegant, painting

items.title: Wine, Cheese, and Fruit
items.description_narrative: John F. Francis's 1857 oil painting presents a detailed still life arrangement of wine, cheese, and various fruits. The careful rendering of textures and forms invites contemplation of the depicted culinary items.
items.tags: still life, food, wine, cheese, fruit, oil painting, 19th century, realism

items.title: Lights of Other Days
items.description_narrative: John Frederick Peto created 'Lights of Other Days' in 1906 using oil on canvas. This artwork, part of the Art Institute of Chicago's collection, invites contemplation of the past through its evocative title.
items.tags: painting, american art, early 20th century, nostalgia, memory, reflection

items.title: A Vanitas Still Life with a Flag, Candlestick, Musical Instruments, Books, Writing Paraphernalia, Globes, and Hourglass
items.description_narrative: This intricate still life by Edwaert Collier meticulously arranges objects such as flags, musical instruments, books, and globes. These elements, alongside a candlestick and hourglass, serve as traditional memento mori, reminding the viewer of life's transience and the futility of worldly pursuits.
items.tags: still life, vanitas, symbolic, memento mori, oil painting, dutch art, objects, allegory

items.title: A Sunday on La Grande Jatte — 1884
items.description_narrative: Georges Seurat's monumental oil on canvas, "A Sunday on La Grande Jatte — 1884," captures Parisians enjoying a leisurely afternoon on an island in the Seine. This iconic work is meticulously composed using the artist's groundbreaking pointillist technique, creating luminous color and form.
items.tags: sunday, leisure, park, pointillism, post-impressionism, Parisian life, serene, vibrant
